top_issues.issue: Floating orange light blobs over the foreground floor
top_issues.why: They read as lens dirt or render artifacts rather than light landing on the floor. They make the room look less cared for.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Remove the foreground blobs, or ground them as soft pools that sit on the floor plane under real sources.

top_issues.issue: Locker and ceiling fixtures ignore the palette
top_issues.why: The beige locker with its orange band and the mixed warm/cool fixtures make each palette look like a wall recolour, not a whole room mood.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Tint the locker body, trim and fixture colour temperature per palette so the whole room shifts together.

top_issues.issue: Rug and radio weak at play scale
top_issues.why: In the default framing the rug is a thin red strip and the radio is clipped by the frame edge, so two bought items barely register.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give the rug more floor depth or a stronger border and pattern at distance. Keep the radio and nightstand inside the mid frame, or give the dial a stronger glow.

top_issues.why: About 40% of the mid frame is bare dark plating, which dilutes the furnished-room richness.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add more floor value variation, such as a warm pool from the portholes, a runner or plating detail, so the foreground supports the room.

top_issues.why: The blanket is one flat slab and the desk is a featureless grey box, which reads less cared for than the kettle and corkboard.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add a fold or turn-down line and a second tone to the blanket. Add a desk lamp pool or a few objects on the desk.
